The control plane (21) joined the drops when slides 3 and 16 grew to carry the 2026-10-26 evidence: it is the surface with no caller, so it is the cheapest thing in the deck to describe in a sentence

protect: **Protect 3, 4, 14, 16, 22 and 23.** Three and four are what make this a comparison rather than a tour; 14 and 16 are the only measured performance claims in the deck; 22 is status and 23 is the asks. Never cut a divider: a cut deck without them is a list of slides. Backups B1 (typed hops) and B2 (compute patterns) are already out of every order - do not put them back to fill time.
say_out_loud: that every REAL run so far is a single lineage, and `replicas > 1` has only ever executed against the mock toolkit - the deck's own mock run in run.json does two lineages per run - never on the six-stage chain; that on the two Rosetta stages we share, our thresholds are **weaker** than the reference pipeline's PROD gates (backlog G4/G5), so the claim is about where the verdict lives and not about strictness; and that every Delta and baseline figure on these slides is transcribed from run archives outside this checkout, named in each slide's footer; that the baseline figures credited on slides 3 and 15 are the reference pipeline's BEST period and not its current one - with the same decision function its own fastrelax pass rate fell 63.6% -> 49.4% between 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-22, and only 1.3 of those 14.2 points is binder length, which this deck states rather than uses; and that the lever this deck does NOT pull is now measured - one policy held fixed at k=1 to k=8 pipelines per GPU is worth x5.52 on backbones per node-hour and x5.11 on high-quality folds per GPU-hour, against about x3 for the best decision layer anybody has run at matched packing, and we are running one lineage on one of four GPUs.
